text:
A 7-3 score suggests a rout, but the chances say otherwise. Colorado and Calgary finished at 2.83 and 2.79 expected goals, with 62 shot attempts against 61, and the replay math calls it a coin flip: COL won 51 percent of simulated games, CGY 49. The Flames actually out-chanced Colorado through the first two periods, 2.19 expected goals to 1.73, yet trailed 4-1 after the second.

The gap came from finishing and goaltending. Devon Toews scored twice, once on a 1 percent chance in the second period, and Cale Makar and Nathan MacKinnon followed with goals on 6 percent chances apiece. Calgary's Devin Cooley allowed seven on 2.83 expected, 4.17 goals worse than an average goalie would have, while Scott Wedgewood gave up three on 2.79 expected, roughly what the shots deserved. Colorado spent most of the night riding its shooting, not controlling play.

The third period tilted toward Colorado, 1.10 expected goals to 0.59, and Makar's slap shot made it 5-1 before Jaden Schwartz added a sixth a minute later. Mikael Backlund and Kevin Bahl cut it to 6-3 within 69 seconds, and Schwartz restored the margin at 9:41 on a 2 percent chance. Makar finished with two goals and an assist and was named the first star, with MacKinnon and Toews behind him. Nobody scored on the power play (0 for 3 for COL, 0 for 2 for CGY), so all ten goals came at even strength.
